why: Tier-1 register write, manager scope — recording operator decisions and PR ownership into docs/claude/work/** is explicitly management, and this touches OPEN-PRS.json and nothing else. It fills a record that was EMPTY: handoff_check graded '17 open PR(s) have no row ... of 60 open, against 0 recorded', meaning a successor manager could see none of the in-flight PRs nor any decision attached to them. 19 rows, reconciled against a live 60-row list_pull_requests observation, with tier and landing read from each branch's OWN .github/pr-landing/<slug>.json rather than inferred. The most useful thing it establishes is a NEGATIVE: every open PR declares tier 1, so not one is waiting on an operator approval, and every operator_decision is the typed verdict not_required with the reasoning written out — which is a positive claim, not a missing record, and is exactly the half-informed case OPEN-PRS.json's own _doc says is more dangerous than a missing row. It also names the three things that are genuinely decisions rather than queue positions: #12072 needs a human content ruling (the row-aware driver refused it because two sessions edited the same backlog row differently), and #12070 and #12219 are drafts on purpose that must not be un-drafted to shorten the queue. open_pr_record.py --strict reports structural=well_formed and decisions=graded.
